{"Author":"doomzao","Name":"True Ping","InternalName":"TruePing","Punchline":"Your real FFXIV ping: the latency you actually feel, with jitter and loss.","Description":"Measures your true FFXIV ping by timing the game's own keepalive round-trip (the latency the server actually answers), not the OS network latency. Because it reads the game protocol, it reports the real latency you feel even when you route through a proxy or VPN, where ordinary ping tools only see localhost. Shows current ping, average, min, max, jitter and packet loss, in a floating overlay and in the server info bar.

Commands:
/trueping : open the settings window

{"Author":"Dasha","Name":"DashaTweaks","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.3.6.0","DalamudApiLevel":15,"Description":"A growing collection of FFXIV quality-of-life tweaks, each in its own settings tab:

- Hotbar Helper: when you open Actions & Traits, scans your hotbars against your current job and shows any actions or role actions you haven't slotted anywhere — then drag an icon straight onto a hotbar slot to assign it.
- Submarines: FC submarine status with per-sub EXP bars, plus a tabbed voyage route planner — EXP/hour levelling routes (with fuel cost), exploration routes that reveal the most still-undiscovered locations, and gil-farming routes (per-sub gil/hour, build and rank requirements) — with one-click apply, optional unlock-progression routing, and auto-repair.
- Leves: automated craft (tradecraft) leve hand-ins — pick a leve, stand at the counter, and it accepts and turns in until your allowance floor or items run out.

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"Gluttony Combo","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.4.310","CategoryTags":null,"Changelog":"v1.0.4.311 (2026-10-18) [testing]
- **Deep Dungeon (Palace of the Dead): the sustaining potion is spent inside a behemoth's Ecliptic Meteor window whatever the health slider says.** The floor-180 meteor takes roughly 80% of maximum health, so a potion held back for after the hit is wasted. The gate now treats the meteor window itself as a heal window and rolls the potion in it; the preset toggle, item readiness and the no-Rehabilitation check all still apply, and the health slider keeps ruling everywhere else. A behemoth tracker recognises the two floor-180 behemoths by name and watches the boss's cast and health for the meteor threshold, exposing a hold band (while the cast nears the threshold) and the window (the cast itself) to the job modules below.
- **Ninja: Shade Shift is banked for the Ecliptic Meteor and pressed in the window.** While the behemoth nears its meteor threshold the shield is no longer spent on its own health or incoming-damage triggers; in the window itself it presses even at full health.
- **Summoner: Radiant Aegis banks and presses around the Ecliptic Meteor.** The overcap rule holds the second charge while the behemoth nears the threshold instead of burning it early; the maintain rule keeps a shield up through the window even above its health slider.
- **Black Mage: Manaward is banked for the Ecliptic Meteor in solo play.** The own-health trigger is held while the behemoth nears the threshold; the incoming-damage trigger still presses the ward for the cast itself, so the window stays covered.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.310 (2026-10-17)

- NIN: fixed a Kassatsu sync issue.
- DTR bar entry: right-click now opens the UI; the auto-rotation toggle moved to left-click.
- PvP: fixed hotbar saving writing to the wrong slot.
- SAM: fixed the FRU opener.
- MCH: removed an unused target setting; job config cleanups across many jobs.

v1.0.4.308 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- Telemetry only, no behaviour change: the Crucible decision log line (CR|) now carries the inputs the offline replay could not rebuild from the rest of the line - the target's invulnerability flag, the readiness of the Beastmaster's long cooldowns (the three horns, Shield Charge, Rally, Cheer, Beast Mode and the rest) as a bitmap, the health potion count, the player's current and maximum health, GCD and weave readiness, the in-combat and casting state, and whether Morphos or other enemies are still up. The offline replay tool reads these fields and replays the Crucible hold rules from them, so more of a recorded fight can be replayed faithfully.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.307 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **Beastmaster in the Crucible of the Unbroken, King Ahriman Piece: the Final Hourglass is no longer broken at the moment that points the Death cone at the character.** Breaking the hourglass makes the needle fire Death, a 23-yard cone along the needle's heading at its next tick, and Death puts Doom on whatever stands in it: a 6-second countdown that ends in certain death and that no cleanse, dispel or item removes. The needle ticks every 1.56 seconds and turns a quarter turn after each tick, and the character stands bound beside the hourglass, so a break lands in the cone about one time in four. The recorded runs show it: Death hit the character in 6 of 12 roulettes and every Doom ended in death. The rotation used to break the hourglass as fast as possible whatever the needle did. Now, once the hourglass is low enough for a single hit to break it (75% of its health or less), the weaponskill is held whenever a needle tick that the break could precede points at the character, and goes out the moment none does; the needle points at the character a quarter of the time, so the wait is at most one turn of the needle (about 6 seconds). The hold gives up 12 seconds after the hourglass appears, and does nothing at all when the needle cannot be read, which leaves the previous behaviour.
- **The log records every turn of the needle (`NE|` lines: the needle's heading, the hourglass's health, the hourglass's age, and the character's bearing and distance from the needle).**
- Doom itself cannot be removed. The game marks the Crucible's Doom as not cleansable ("Certain death when counter reaches zero"): no beast action (Ultrasonics, Scouring Ash, Quelling Wave) and no Crucible item removes it, so the cleanse path correctly stays idle. Its Crucible sources are Mortal Ray and the Ahriman gaze (Taurus Piece; the lit floor tiles clear it), the Dirty Eye's Mortal Gaze (looking away avoids it) and the King Ahriman Piece's Death (fixed here); Soulreaper's Armor is the only item that resists Doom.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.306 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **White Mage: Temperance and Divine Caress are now handled as the two separate actions they are.** Since the pair was split, the heal combos watched for the Divine Grace buff and pressed whatever Temperance had turned into. Now Temperance itself is used when it is ready - in the single-target, area and simple heal modes and in the raidwide features alike - and Divine Caress is pressed on its own when it is ready. The area-of-effect simple heal mode gains a Divine Caress step it did not have, and the Asylum replacement mode now tries Asylum first, then Temperance, then Divine Caress, instead of preferring Temperance while Asylum was on cooldown.
- **A ground-placed action is no longer fired before it is ready.** The action watcher could send a ground-target placement for a replacement action that was still on cooldown; it now checks readiness first.
- Merges upstream WrathCombo changes through 2026-10-14 (9 commits). The automatic regen and shield checks on the focus target now use the plugin's own status lookup, ending an ambiguity with the shared library's lookup of the same name.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.305 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **Beastmaster in the Crucible of the Unbroken, Abaddon Piece: the rotation no longer stands idle while a Morpho is alive.** The Abaddon was held back from the start of the fight until every Morpho was gone, and the Morphos themselves are never attacked, so for as long as a Morpho lived (over a minute in a recorded fight) the Abaddon was the only enemy and nothing was left that the rotation was allowed to hit: no damage and no aggro while the Morphos confused the character. Intended behaviour in this piece: the Drake and the Barbmoles are killed first, as before; once the Abaddon is the only enemy left it is attacked and chipped down to 35% of its health, and held there while any Morpho is alive, so it is never killed ahead of the Morphos it feeds on; once the last Morpho is gone it is attacked to the end. Eggs and Morphos as targets are still never attacked, and the Gigantis gel rule is unchanged.
- The Abaddon's Regen (Rehabilitation, one minute, renewed each time it eats a Morpho) is deliberately not dispelled: Quelling Wave never removed it in the recorded casts (15 casts on the Abaddon, the buff always ran its full minute), so the rotation does not spend casts on it. The Drake's Blaze Spikes are still dispelled.

{"Author":"Valenth Siveria","Name":"I Am Ready","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"1.1.0.0","Changelog":"API15 finally","DalamudApiLevel":"15","Description":"# I Am Ready

**I Am Ready** is a Dalamud plugin for Final Fantasy XIV that automatically accepts or declines Party and Alliance Ready Checks based on a customizable counter. 

Whether you are stepping away for a moment or just tired of clicking, this plugin handles ready checks for you while mimicking human reaction times.

## ✨ Features

* **Auto-Answer Ready Checks:** Automatically clicks "Yes" or "No" when a ready check appears.
* **Configurable "Yes" Counter:** Set a specific number of times you want to automatically answer "Yes". Once that limit is reached, the plugin will automatically start answering "No" to prevent pulling when you are actually away.
* **Natural Delay:** Enable a randomized delay (0.7 to 2.5 seconds) before the plugin answers, making it look like a natural human reaction.
* **Smart Chat Triggers (Regex):** Add custom text phrases to the plugin. If someone says one of these phrases in Party or Alliance chat (e.g., "reset", "pulling"), your counter will automatically reset back to zero.
* **Bilingual Support:** The user interface is available in both English and German.

## 🚀 Usage

1. Type `/iar` in the in-game chat to open the configuration window.
2. Click the **Inactive/Active** button at the top to turn the auto-responder on or off.
3. Adjust the **Yes Count** slider. For example, if set to `5`, the plugin will answer "Yes" to the next 5 ready checks, and "No" to any checks after that.
4. Click the **Start** button at any time to manually reset your current counter back to zero.

### Chat Triggers (Regex Patterns)
At the bottom of the window, you can expand the **Regex Patterns** section. Here you can add simple words or complex regex patterns. 
If the plugin reads a matching message in your Party or Cross-World Party chat, it will instantly reset your counter to zero, assuming a new pull or instance is starting!

- **Market-price lookups no longer log warnings while they retry.** When Universalis is slow or busy it answers with a temporary "try again" status or takes longer than before; the price client already retries those on its own with a pause between tries - that is its designed behavior, not a fault, so those lines now go to the debug log. Only one warning is written when a batch gives up entirely after all retries, and stale cached prices are used meanwhile, exactly as before.
- **The price client now waits up to 60 seconds per request instead of 20.** Under load, Universalis sometimes finishes a large price query just after the old 20-second cutoff; the request was cancelled while the server was still working on it and the prices for that batch were refetched from scratch. The longer budget lets those queries land.
- Market-price log lines no longer paste a hundred item numbers into the log; a batch is described as its item count instead.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Full harness: 401/401 PASS (6 new).

v0.1.7.8 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Knightshopper no longer buys units that are sitting on a retainer.** The purchase target counted everything the catalog can see, but the fetch-from-retainer step runs after the purchase and brings those units in anyway - with 90 units on a retainer, none in the bags and 9 missing, the run bought 99 instead of 9. The target now counts what is physically in the bags, and the fetch tops the bags up to exactly what the cart needs; every currency routes on the same corrected target.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Full harness: 395/395 PASS (4 new).

v0.1.7.7 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Cart dispatches can hand vendor purchases to Knightshopper.** When a dispatch is missing materials that a vendor sells - gil vendors, and currency vendors priced in one currency Knightshopper supports - the run groups that list by currency and buys it through Knightshopper's purchase IPC at target inventory totals, before any shopping stop fires. The run prints each group, its currency and the estimated total cost before anything is spent. Market-board items are never routed, and one attempt per group means a refused purchase never retries; a repeat dispatch asks for the same target totals at most, so nothing is ever bought twice.

Purchases also need LazyCrafter on Knightshopper's allowed-plugins IPC list, which is set in Knightshopper's own settings (IPC permissions); LazyCrafter never changes Knightshopper's settings. The new switch (on by default) is "Buy vendor items through Knightshopper during a dispatch" in the settings.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- With the switch off, or without Knightshopper installed, the run behaves exactly as before.
- Full harness: 391/391 PASS (16 new).

- The cart-run hand-off switches can only be changed while no cart run is active.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"LazyCrucible","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.9.5","CategoryTags":["jobs","utility"],"Changelog":"v0.1.9.16 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **"Score: three familiars" run-roster mode, off by default.** For score runs. A run roster of one to three familiars scores the Beast Squad III bonus on every board, so with the option on the run roster is the best three familiars for the whole board instead of the board's full roster. The three are chosen from the familiars you own and that are not knocked out: they cover as many of the board's required interrupt, dispel and cleanse needs as any three can, then the damage the board calls to be blunted, then three of one kin when that costs no required cover (the Gambit bonus), then the rest by points. A roster of three saved for a different board is rewritten for the board you enter. Whatever the three cannot answer on the board is named on the window's summary line; nothing pops up. With three or fewer familiars the game registers the battlehorns itself, so the plugin leaves them alone. Found in the settings window and the Lazy Hub as "Score: three familiars".
- With the option off, nothing changes. While AutoDuty drives the run roster the plugin stands by there, option on or off.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.9.15 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **Mitigation in the horn picks.** Fights with a damage wall now field a familiar that blunts it, ranked below every interrupt, dispel and cleanse need, and counted only for a familiar above the danger HP line. Durga's Atomic Ray gets a magic answer (drake's Smoldering Scales, pugil's Water Wall or a Scalekin's Scaleskin); Borgny gets coblyn's Vulcanize for the poison plus a magic answer; Gargoyle's Sweeping Evisceration gets a physical answer (a Beastkin's Beastskin, coblyn's Vulcanize or adamantoise's Harden Shell). The fight guide lists these under "Calls for".
- One telemetry line per fight names the team on the horns and the needs it cannot answer (`uncovered=`).
- **Works with AutoDuty.** While AutoDuty runs, it handles the run roster, shop, treasure, spoils and campsite itself, so the plugin stands by there; the battlehorns are AutoDuty's only with its "Fight picks" on, and the plugin picks them otherwise. AutoDuty's active profile is read through AutoDuty's own interface (its config file when that is unavailable), never changed; when neither can be read, every screen stands by, as before. - **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the "Sit while fishing" switch to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.5.0 (2026-09-25)

- Persistent seating across fishing hole visits: if the character stands up during a visit to a fishing hole (such as putting the rod away to change bait or use cordials, or manually standing up), the automation now detects the stand and re-seats upon resuming fishing or on the subsequent cast.
- Unaccepted send cap: the 3-send limit per hole visit is now scoped to consecutive unaccepted sends rather than a lifetime cap per hole visit. When a sit is accepted by the game, the counter resets, ensuring long fishing sessions with multiple bait changes or pauses remain seated while still guarding against unbounded retry loops if commands are blocked.

v0.1.4.0 (2026-09-25)

- Sits after a cast: the automated /sit check now runs after a cast once the line is settled in the water (`LineInWater`), in addition to the pre-cast standby beat (`PoleReady`). In active fishing loops or when using automated casting tools, the standby beat between casts typically lasts under a second, which previously prevented the automation from ever triggering across repeated casts (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsStandbyBeat`).
- Safe timing: commands are sent only after the line has been in the water for at least 1 second to ensure the cast animation has resolved, and continue to be refused during active casting, biting, hooking, reeling, and position change animations.

v0.1.3.0 (2026-09-05)

- Correction first, because the last release's notes got the game wrong: FFXIV does NOT force standing on every hooked fish. If the character is sitting when the cast starts, the game keeps it seated for the whole loop - a hook may cause a momentary stand, but the game sits back down on its own. v0.1.2.0 was designed around that mistake (one /sit per cast) and this release replaces it entirely.
- Sit once, then stay out of the way. The plugin now sends a single /sit per fishing trip, at a moment the game will actually accept it, and then does nothing for the rest of the trip (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Decide`).
- That moment is the standby beat: rod out, no line in the water (`FishingEventHandler.State == PoleReady`), held for a second, at least 3 seconds clear of a bite/hook/reel, with the character read as standing for 3 seconds straight. It will never fire mid-cast, with a line in the water, mid-bite, mid-reel, or while already sitting down or standing up (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsStandbyBeat`).
- That is why v0.1.1.0 looked like it did nothing: it sent its one /sit the instant the fishing flag came on, which is after the line is already out, and the game swallows the emote there - ten sends across ten sessions, no effect. v0.1.2.0 still counted "line in water" as a valid moment and would have done the same thing.
- No re-sit after every cast, ever. A brief standing read just after a bite, hook, reel or collectable prompt is treated as the game's own animation, not as the character standing up, so the plugin does nothing and lets the game re-seat (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsHookish`).
- A "trip" is one visit to a fishing hole, not one cast. The fishing flag drops between casts (v0.1.1.0 saw ten "sessions" in 21 minutes), so the limits are now anchored to the hole and only reset after 20 seconds away from it (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `StartTrip` / `EndTrip`).
- Anti-yo-yo guards, all hard, because a /sit on a seated character STANDS them: never sends while any seated signal reads seated; at least 10 seconds between sends; at most 3 sends per trip with a log line when it stops; and once the game has taken a sit this trip it will not send again unless the seated read has proved it still reports seated with the rod out (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Decide`, guards 1-5).
- The settings window now shows the trip counters: whether the character is at a hole, sits used out of 3, whether the game took the sit, and whether the seated read works while fishing (file: `ConfigWindow.cs`).
- Removed the "check interval" slider. The plugin now looks every frame, because every limit that matters is a real time limit (10 seconds between sends, 3 seconds of standing before it believes the read, 3 sends a trip) and a 2-second poll just made it step over short standby beats between quick casts. Saved values are ignored, not lost (files: `ConfigWindow.cs`, `Configuration.cs`).
- The policy is now a plain C# class with no game code in it (`Core/SitPolicy.cs`), replayed offline against 26 scripted fishing sessions by `tests/LazyFishSitter.Harness`. Three releases in a row shipped a rule that only broke in game; the harness caught three more before this one shipped, including a dead window that would have stopped a refused /sit from ever being retried.
- Keeps the detailed state logging (every fishing-state and posture change, 40 lines a minute max) and adds a one-line trip summary, so the still-open question - does the game ever report seated while a line is out - can be answered from the log without typing anything in game (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `EndTrip`).

- SUPERSEDED BY v0.1.3.0 AND NEVER FISHED ON: the design premise below was wrong. It claimed the game forces standing on every hooked fish; it does not - if the character was sitting before the hook, the game re-seats automatically. Everything in this entry that follows from that premise (a /sit per stand episode) was removed in v0.1.3.0. Kept here for the record only.
- Re-sat after every cast and every catch, on the mistaken premise above: the unit was a "stand episode" (fishing start, or the fishing state machine passing through Hooking/ReleasingCatch/ConfirmingCollectable), and each episode got at most ONE /sit (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Arm` / `TrackTransitions`).
- Sent only when it believed the game would accept it: read `EventFramework.Instance()->EventHandlerModule.FishingEventHandler` (FFXIVClientStructs) and required `State` to be `PoleReady` or `LineInWater` for at least 1 s with `ChangingPosition` false. Counting `LineInWater` as acceptable was the second defect - that is exactly where the emote gets swallowed (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Tick`).
- Proof the sit took: `FishingEventHandler.ChangingPosition` going true within 3 s of the send was logged as `game accepted our sit`, with a 3 s outcome line per send. This part was correct and is kept in v0.1.3.0 (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `TrackTransitions`).
- No detector-driven re-arm: a "not seated" read after a sit never triggered a re-send on its own (that is what yo-yoed v0.1.0.0). Also kept in v0.1.3.0, hardened (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Tick`).
- Logged every posture/fishing state CHANGE at Information, rate-limited to 40 lines/min: Fishing flag, FishingState, ChangingPosition, CanFish, Character.Mode/ModeParam, EmoteController.EmoteId, GetPosture(), and the combined SEATED verdict (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `TrackTransitions`, `LogTransition`).
- A failing FFXIVClientStructs signature (EventFramework or GetPosture) is logged once at Warning instead of being swallowed silently every check (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Read`).
- Added the shared in-game "What's new" popup (repo standing rule): after an update this changelog opens once; `/lazyfishsitter changelog` reopens it (files: `Plugin.cs`, `Configuration.cs` `LastSeenChangelogVersion`, `LazyFishSitter.csproj` compiles `src/Shared/LalaChangelog`).

v0.1.1.0 (2026-09-05)

- Fixed the sit/stand yo-yo: the seated check compared Character.Mode against raw bytes 12/13, which are RaceChocobo/TripleTriad in FFXIVClientStructs, so the player was never seen as seated and /sit was re-sent every check, and /sit while seated makes the character STAND (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `ReadPosture`; was `IsInPostureLoop`). Now compares against the `CharacterModes` enum (`EmoteLoop` = ground /sit, `InPositionLoop` = chair/bench/pose) - no raw bytes.
- Added a second, independent seated signal: the game's own `EmoteController.GetPosture()` (`SittingOnGround` / `SittingInChair`), so detection works even if Mode reads Gathering while a line is cast; either signal counts as seated (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `ReadPosture`).
- Belt and braces per fishing session: after one /sit has been sent, another is only sent once a posture read has confirmed the sit took AND the player has then read as not-seated on 2 consecutive checks; if the posture read never confirms, at most ONE /sit goes out per continuous Fishing session (re-arms when the Fishing condition drops). - `/lazyfishsitter debug` now prints Mode (name + byte), ModeParam, EmoteController.EmoteId, the game posture, and the per-session counters so the seated-while-fishing question can be settled from the Dalamud log (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `LogDebugState`).","DalamudApiLevel":15,"Description":"Checks every few seconds while you are fishing; if you are not sitting, it runs /sit for you. - **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers auto-eating, "Only in combat duties", the minutes of food left before eating again and the low-food warning with its count to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.5.0 (2026-09-21)

- **"Only eat in combat duties" now covers Crucible of the Unbroken.** The five boards count as combat duties, and so does the Bentbranch Meadows entry area while playing Beastmaster (the one job that can enter), so the meal is eaten before a run starts. Eating before entry matters: a meal eaten inside does not refill HP to the raised maximum.

v0.1.4.0 (2026-09-05)

- Optional decision diagnostics, off by default. Turn on "Log food decisions" (settings window, Advanced / Diagnostics) or run `/lazyfoodbuff telemetry on`, and every time the plugin settles on a food for the current job it writes one line to the plugin log: the food it picked, its score, and the runner-ups it beat — plus a second line when that food is actually eaten. The point is the runner-ups: "picked X at 41.20 over Y at 40.80" is the shape of evidence that can eventually say whether the auto-select weights are right. Nothing leaves the machine; the lines only go to the local plugin log.

- Honest caveat: this is a data-collection investment, not an answer. The outcome side (what a food actually did to damage) needs weeks of encounter data before it says anything statistically — the plugin log will quietly accumulate the decision half in the meantime.
- Nothing about food selection changed. When the toggle is off, the only cost is one boolean read.

v0.1.3.1 (2026-09-05)

- The "What's new" popup now opens after this very update. 0.1.3.0 stayed silent the first time it ran because it had no record of the last version shown; the gate now tells an updated plugin (settings file already present) apart from a brand-new install (none yet) and only the latter stays quiet (`ChangelogGate.Options.ExistingInstall`, read from `pi.ConfigFile.Exists`.

- Nothing else changed. The notes can be reopened later with `/lazyfoodbuff changelog`.

v0.1.3.0 (2026-09-05)

- In-game "What's new" popup. After every update, the first time the character is logged in and out of combat, LazyFoodBuff opens a window with the release notes for every version since the last one shown. It appears once per update; pressing "Got it" (or closing it) keeps it quiet until the next update.
- `/lazyfoodbuff changelog` (or `whatsnew`) reopens the release notes at any time.
- "Open changelog on GitHub" button in the popup links to the full CHANGELOG for this plugin.

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"Lazy Market Companion","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.2.8.15","CategoryTags":["utility"],"Changelog":"v0.2.8.16 (2026-10-17) [testing]
- **Fresh installs no longer show an import notice for a plugin that was never installed.** A leftover line in the configuration loader set the "imported from Dagobert Price Matcher" flag true on every load that created a new configuration, so a brand-new install showed the import notice and the uninstall hint even though no settings were ever imported. The flag now keeps its false default; a genuine import from a found Dagobert configuration still sets it, and the load log's imported= field reports the real value.
- Untried build: tested offline against the plugin's offline test suite, not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.15 (2026-10-10) [testing]
- **The Auto-Market panel's two filter dropdowns remember their setting between sessions.** The status filter (every stack / on the list / not on the list / excluded) and the market-category filter used to reset to "every stack, every category" every time the plugin loaded or the game restarted; they now save as soon as they are changed and come back that way. A saved category the current bags do not contain still shows as "every category" instead of silently hiding everything, and the saved choice comes back when the bags hold that category again.
- Untried build: tested offline against a saved-configuration round trip (the plugin's offline test suite), not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.14 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **A pinch row that cannot get its dialog or its price is now skipped; it no longer aborts the whole retainer with the price dialog left open.** Each row step waits for a dialog or a market price. When one never arrived, the wait ran into the task manager's hard 10-second limit, which discards every remaining task of the run and leaves the dialog on screen. Each row step now has a shorter budget of its own: when it runs out, the row is skipped with a log line naming the stage and row, the row's dialogs are closed, any late market reply is dropped, and the run carries on with the next row. A skipped row keeps its current price.
- **A Universalis timeout is no longer mistaken for a cancellation.** The sale-history lookup used when the market board is empty (and the data-center price lookup) swallowed the HTTP client's own 8-second timeout as if the run had been cancelled, so no answer was ever delivered and the row waited out the hard limit. A timeout is now reported as a failed lookup ("Universalis did not answer in time") and the row falls back to the normal no-price handling.
- **The empty-board sale-history wait now actually times out.** Its 6-second deadline could never be reached because the pending candidate price was cleared on every retry; the candidate is now kept while the lookup is pending.
- **A run that does stop (a step timeout, a session cap, a vendoring halt) closes what it left open before AutoRetainer is handed back.** The price dialog, item menu, market result, sell list and retainer inventory panel are closed innermost-first within a few seconds, the retainer menu is left for AutoRetainer, and the buyback-abandon confirm is never touched. The log names the last stage and what was closed.
- **The AutoRetainer session cap grows with the number of rows the session queued** instead of staying a flat five minutes, so a long pinch list at slow market-board delays is not cut off.
- **A manual sweep that reaches a retainer's buyback-abandon confirm now parks there with a plain report** instead of letting the next retainer's click wait out the hard limit and abort with a generic timeout. The report names the retainers that did not run.
- **An interrupted manual sweep can be resumed.** Starting the sweep again within 30 minutes runs only the retainers that had not finished; retainers that finished are not re-priced.
- Untried build: the guard was tested offline against a simulated task chain and the plugin source, not yet in the game.

- **Fresh installs no longer show an import notice for a plugin that was never installed.** A leftover line in the configuration loader set the "imported from Dagobert Price Matcher" flag true on every load that created a new configuration, so a brand-new install showed the import notice and the uninstall hint even though no settings were ever imported. - **The Auto-Market panel's two filter dropdowns remember their setting between sessions.** The status filter (every stack / on the list / not on the list / excluded) and the market-category filter used to reset to "every stack, every category" every time the plugin loaded or the game restarted; they now save as soon as they are changed and come back that way. A saved category the current bags do not contain still shows as "every category" instead of silently hiding everything, and the saved choice comes back when the bags hold that category again.

v0.2.8.14 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **A pinch row that cannot get its dialog or its price is now skipped; it no longer aborts the whole retainer with the price dialog left open.** Each row step waits for a dialog or a market price. When one never arrived, the wait ran into the task manager's hard 10-second limit, which discards every remaining task of the run and leaves the dialog on screen. Each row step now has a shorter budget of its own: when it runs out, the row is skipped with a log line naming the stage and row, the row's dialogs are closed, any late market reply is dropped, and the run carries on with the next row. A skipped row keeps its current price.
- **A Universalis timeout is no longer mistaken for a cancellation.** The sale-history lookup used when the market board is empty (and the data-center price lookup) swallowed the HTTP client's own 8-second timeout as if the run had been cancelled, so no answer was ever delivered and the row waited out the hard limit. A timeout is now reported as a failed lookup ("Universalis did not answer in time") and the row falls back to the normal no-price handling.
- **The empty-board sale-history wait now actually times out.** Its 6-second deadline could never be reached because the pending candidate price was cleared on every retry; the candidate is now kept while the lookup is pending.
- **A run that does stop (a step timeout, a session cap, a vendoring halt) closes what it left open before AutoRetainer is handed back.** The price dialog, item menu, market result, sell list and retainer inventory panel are closed innermost-first within a few seconds, the retainer menu is left for AutoRetainer, and the buyback-abandon confirm is never touched. The log names the last stage and what was closed.
- **The AutoRetainer session cap grows with the number of rows the session queued** instead of staying a flat five minutes, so a long pinch list at slow market-board delays is not cut off.
- **A manual sweep that reaches a retainer's buyback-abandon confirm now parks there with a plain report** instead of letting the next retainer's click wait out the hard limit and abort with a generic timeout. The report names the retainers that did not run.
- **An interrupted manual sweep can be resumed.** Starting the sweep again within 30 minutes runs only the retainers that had not finished; retainers that finished are not re-priced.
- Untried build: the guard was tested offline against a simulated task chain and the plugin source, not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the switch that serves retainer data (the port stays in the plugin's own window) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.0.1 (2026-09-05)


- Corrected a wrong claim in the v0.1.0.0 notes below (and on the mod's web page): **the endpoint does not answer 503 on logout.** Once logged in, it keeps serving that character's last known retainer state - including at the title screen - and only ever answers 503 if it has never read the retainer table at all since the plugin loaded (i.e. it started at the title screen and no login has happened yet). That freeze is deliberate and is the better behaviour: measured previously the frozen live snapshot was still *newer* than AutoRetainer's file, so falling back to the file on logout would have shown the dashboard **older** data, not fresher. No behaviour was changed here - only the description was wrong.
- The settings window no longer reports "serving live snapshot" while logged out. It now distinguishes three states: no snapshot yet, serving a live snapshot, or serving the last-known snapshot while the game is in transition.


- For anything scripting against this endpoint: `readAt` is the time the request was **served**, not the time the data was read from the game, so it does not reveal how stale a frozen snapshot is. Use the settings window (or `/lazyretainerlive debug`) to tell live from frozen.

v0.1.0.0 (2026-09-05)


- First release. LazyRetainerLive reads the logged-in character's LIVE retainer table (the same in-memory data AutoRetainer uses to drive its own countdowns) and serves it as JSON on `http://127.0.0.1:10504/retainers`, so the ffxiv dashboard's retainer panel can show venture countdowns that update the moment a venture is collected instead of whenever AutoRetainer next saves its config file.
- When not logged in (or the live table has no data yet) the endpoint answers HTTP 503, which tells the dashboard relay to fall back to AutoRetainer's file. Loopback only - the port is never reachable from other machines.


- Companion of AutoRetainer - it reads, it never writes, assigns, or collects anything. Settings: Enabled (default on) and loopback port (default 10504). Commands: `/lazyretainerlive` opens settings, `/lazyretainerlive debug` dumps listener + snapshot state, `/lazyretainerlive changelog` reopens this popup.
- Why this exists: AutoRetainer's `DefaultConfig.json` (which feeds the dashboard today) is saved only at AutoRetainer's own save points, so its venture rows can be tens of minutes stale while ventures are actually completing. {"Author":"Akari","Name":"Mahjong Advisor","AcceptsFeedback":true,"ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.3.10.0","CanUnloadAsync":false,"CategoryTags":["Utility"],"Changelog":"v0.3.10.0: Silent-endgame defence. The threat model measured a silent opponent as at most 19% likely tenpai, so on a table with no riichi and no melds every safety rule stayed off - the controller pushed one-away hands with 6-9 tiles left to draw into damaten twice in one match (4,200 and 2,200 deal-ins) and paid full tsumo on 14,300 and 20,000 hands. Silent seats now take on a readiness floor that rises from zero at wall 32 to a concrete threat at wall 16, arming the existing late-wall fold and per-tile safety ranking on quiet tables. v0.3.9.0: Chi freeze fixed. The shape-selection dialog ignores scripted call picks (confirmed by the first picker dump), so chi now only fires when exactly one shape is possible - that path completes with no dialog. Multi-shape chi passes instead of stalling; the pass log records how many shapes were declined. v0.3.8.0: Late-wall defence. When an opponent is a concrete threat and the wall is down to the last four go-arounds, the controller folds any hand that is not tenpai instead of pushing a 1-shanten no-riichi hand. This was the 12,000 deal-in in the first match. Diagnostic bundles now also include chi picker dumps. The end-of-match results screen still waits for you by design - that is the one click after a match. v0.3.7.0: Chi is now fully automated. The controller calls chi when the advisor ranks it best, and if the client shows the shape-selection surface it fires the first variant and re-evaluates the hand. The picker layout is dumped once per session to the log folder so shape-specific selection can be refined against real captures. A v6 config migration enables chi. v0.3.6.0: Read each opponent meld strip independently. A hidden empty strip for one quiet seat no longer suppresses every visible meld on the table, so the threat model sees called sets when they exist. This is a readiness/defence accuracy change; automation logic is unchanged. v0.3.5.0: Fix the second freeze. A complete open hand is no longer assumed to be a legal tsumo: the controller checks for an actual yaku and keeps discarding when there is none. Call prompts now prefer the newest board addition over a possibly stale pond tile (the live log claimed 6z/dragon while the actual Pon was 9m), and the log records the last discard tile/seat. A v5 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging. v0.3.4.0: Fix the self-kan freeze. A Kan/Pass bar at state 6 is ignored and the normal discard proceeds instead of firing a Pass callback the client ignores. Session stats are preserved after /mjadv stop so the bundle still shows the run, and a v4 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging for the next launch. v0.3.3.0: Reset the exposed tuning sliders to the fitted win-rate defaults (base hand value 1300, deal-in 5200, noten 1500, opponent hand 4000) with a one-time v3 config migration. Diagnostic bundles now include the actual Dalamud plugin config file from pluginConfigs. v0.3.2.0: State 15 is now treated as the generic other-players state unless real call buttons are present, state 22 (forced riichi discard) is automated, and state 27 (between-hands result/score) is recognised instead of showing stale advice. Overlay/advice are now gated to actual decision states, and diagnostic bundles can read the Dalamud log while it is open. v0.3.1.0: Auto-play and file logging are now on by default, /mjadv session starts a clean logged session, and /mjadv bundle packages the recent JSONL logs, config, layouts, Dalamud log tail and a full last-read snapshot into one zip. Status changes are now logged as auto-status records. v0.3.0.1: Re-arm auto-play on a state change even when the hand happens to repeat, and wait for the Riichi/Pass prompt to close before cutting the riichi tile. v0.3.0.0: Optional auto-play. Replays the client's FireCallback protocol for discards, calls, riichi, ron/tsumo and result advancement, using the reference solver's live-verified handshake and timing guards. Off by default; /mjadv auto [on/off] or /mjadv stop toggles it. Pon/ron/tsumo/riichi are enabled by default, chi and kan are opt-in, the chi shape picker pauses for a manual choice, and the new-hand screen is never auto-advanced. Added /mjadv hand and /mjadv options diagnostics. v0.2.0.2: Keep the previous wall count, so the wall-jump half of new-hand detection actually fires. v0.2.0.1: Reset the pond baselines at the start of a new hand, so the first discard of the hand is tracked and the first call prompt gets the right claimed tile. v0.2.0.0: Meld containers now read by default (112-115 families), with a fail-closed check against our own called-meld count. Own meld tiles are recovered from hand deltas when nodes are unavailable, so ukeire no longer counts tiles already in a call. Riichi detection is marker-node only; the dead rotation and score-drop paths are gone. One node-tree walk per read instead of up to seven. Fixed dead hands getting a nonzero win rate and Pass inventing a yaku path. Red-five decoding accepts both absolute and alias ids. Removed the obsolete fold-threshold setting. Setup window no longer reopens every launch. v1.0.4.311 (2026-10-18) [testing]

- **Summoner: Radiant Aegis banks and presses around the Ecliptic Meteor.** The overcap rule holds the second charge while the behemoth nears the threshold instead of burning it early; the maintain rule keeps a shield up through the window even above its health slider.
- **Black Mage: Manaward is banked for the Ecliptic Meteor in solo play.** The own-health trigger is held while the behemoth nears the threshold; the incoming-damage trigger still presses the ward for the cast itself, so the window stays covered.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.310 (2026-10-17)

- NIN: fixed a Kassatsu sync issue.
- DTR bar entry: right-click now opens the UI; the auto-rotation toggle moved to left-click.
- PvP: fixed hotbar saving writing to the wrong slot.
- SAM: fixed the FRU opener.
- MCH: removed an unused target setting; job config cleanups across many jobs.

v1.0.4.308 (2026-10-15) [testing]

The offline replay tool reads these fields and replays the Crucible hold rules from them, so more of a recorded fight can be replayed faithfully.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.307 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **Beastmaster in the Crucible of the Unbroken, King Ahriman Piece: the Final Hourglass is no longer broken at the moment that points the Death cone at the character.** Breaking the hourglass makes the needle fire Death, a 23-yard cone along the needle's heading at its next tick, and Death puts Doom on whatever stands in it: a 6-second countdown that ends in certain death and that no cleanse, dispel or item removes. The needle ticks every 1.56 seconds and turns a quarter turn after each tick, and the character stands bound beside the hourglass, so a break lands in the cone about one time in four. The recorded runs show it: Death hit the character in 6 of 12 roulettes and every Doom ended in death. The rotation used to break the hourglass as fast as possible whatever the needle did. Now, once the hourglass is low enough for a single hit to break it (75% of its health or less), the weaponskill is held whenever a needle tick that the break could precede points at the character, and goes out the moment none does; the needle points at the character a quarter of the time, so the wait is at most one turn of the needle (about 6 seconds). The hold gives up 12 seconds after the hourglass appears, and does nothing at all when the needle cannot be read, which leaves the previous behaviour.
- **The log records every turn of the needle (`NE|` lines: the needle's heading, the hourglass's health, the hourglass's age, and the character's bearing and distance from the needle).**
- Doom itself cannot be removed. The game marks the Crucible's Doom as not cleansable ("Certain death when counter reaches zero"): no beast action (Ultrasonics, Scouring Ash, Quelling Wave) and no Crucible item removes it, so the cleanse path correctly stays idle. Its Crucible sources are Mortal Ray and the Ahriman gaze (Taurus Piece; the lit floor tiles clear it), the Dirty Eye's Mortal Gaze (looking away avoids it) and the King Ahriman Piece's Death (fixed here); Soulreaper's Armor is the only item that resists Doom.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. {"Author":"dajoey","Name":"Gluttony Combo","Punchline":"Lalalazy fork of Wrath Combo - XIVCombo for very lazy players.","Description":"Gluttony Combo - lalalazy fork of Gluttony Combo. XIVCombo for very lazy players.","InternalName":"GluttonyCombo","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.4.310","Changelog":"v1.0.4.311 (2026-10-18) [testing]
- **Deep Dungeon (Palace of the Dead): the sustaining potion is spent inside a behemoth's Ecliptic Meteor window whatever the health slider says.** The floor-180 meteor takes roughly 80% of maximum health, so a potion held back for after the hit is wasted. The gate now treats the meteor window itself as a heal window and rolls the potion in it; the preset toggle, item readiness and the no-Rehabilitation check all still apply, and the health slider keeps ruling everywhere else. A behemoth tracker recognises the two floor-180 behemoths by name and watches the boss's cast and health for the meteor threshold, exposing a hold band (while the cast nears the threshold) and the window (the cast itself) to the job modules below.
- **Ninja: Shade Shift is banked for the Ecliptic Meteor and pressed in the window.** While the behemoth nears its meteor threshold the shield is no longer spent on its own health or incoming-damage triggers; in the window itself it presses even at full health.
- **Summoner: Radiant Aegis banks and presses around the Ecliptic Meteor.** The overcap rule holds the second charge while the behemoth nears the threshold instead of burning it early; the maintain rule keeps a shield up through the window even above its health slider.
- **Black Mage: Manaward is banked for the Ecliptic Meteor in solo play.** The own-health trigger is held while the behemoth nears the threshold; the incoming-damage trigger still presses the ward for the cast itself, so the window stays covered.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.310 (2026-10-17)

- NIN: fixed a Kassatsu sync issue.
- DTR bar entry: right-click now opens the UI; the auto-rotation toggle moved to left-click.
- PvP: fixed hotbar saving writing to the wrong slot.
- SAM: fixed the FRU opener.
- MCH: removed an unused target setting; job config cleanups across many jobs.

v1.0.4.308 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- Telemetry only, no behaviour change: the Crucible decision log line (CR|) now carries the inputs the offline replay could not rebuild from the rest of the line - the target's invulnerability flag, the readiness of the Beastmaster's long cooldowns (the three horns, Shield Charge, Rally, Cheer, Beast Mode and the rest) as a bitmap, the health potion count, the player's current and maximum health, GCD and weave readiness, the in-combat and casting state, and whether Morphos or other enemies are still up. The offline replay tool reads these fields and replays the Crucible hold rules from them, so more of a recorded fight can be replayed faithfully.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.307 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **Beastmaster in the Crucible of the Unbroken, King Ahriman Piece: the Final Hourglass is no longer broken at the moment that points the Death cone at the character.** Breaking the hourglass makes the needle fire Death, a 23-yard cone along the needle's heading at its next tick, and Death puts Doom on whatever stands in it: a 6-second countdown that ends in certain death and that no cleanse, dispel or item removes. The needle ticks every 1.56 seconds and turns a quarter turn after each tick, and the character stands bound beside the hourglass, so a break lands in the cone about one time in four. The recorded runs show it: Death hit the character in 6 of 12 roulettes and every Doom ended in death. The rotation used to break the hourglass as fast as possible whatever the needle did. Now, once the hourglass is low enough for a single hit to break it (75% of its health or less), the weaponskill is held whenever a needle tick that the break could precede points at the character, and goes out the moment none does; the needle points at the character a quarter of the time, so the wait is at most one turn of the needle (about 6 seconds). The hold gives up 12 seconds after the hourglass appears, and does nothing at all when the needle cannot be read, which leaves the previous behaviour.
- **The log records every turn of the needle (`NE|` lines: the needle's heading, the hourglass's health, the hourglass's age, and the character's bearing and distance from the needle).**
- Doom itself cannot be removed. The game marks the Crucible's Doom as not cleansable ("Certain death when counter reaches zero"): no beast action (Ultrasonics, Scouring Ash, Quelling Wave) and no Crucible item removes it, so the cleanse path correctly stays idle. Its Crucible sources are Mortal Ray and the Ahriman gaze (Taurus Piece; the lit floor tiles clear it), the Dirty Eye's Mortal Gaze (looking away avoids it) and the King Ahriman Piece's Death (fixed here); Soulreaper's Armor is the only item that resists Doom.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.306 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **White Mage: Temperance and Divine Caress are now handled as the two separate actions they are.** Since the pair was split, the heal combos watched for the Divine Grace buff and pressed whatever Temperance had turned into. Now Temperance itself is used when it is ready - in the single-target, area and simple heal modes and in the raidwide features alike - and Divine Caress is pressed on its own when it is ready. The area-of-effect simple heal mode gains a Divine Caress step it did not have, and the Asylum replacement mode now tries Asylum first, then Temperance, then Divine Caress, instead of preferring Temperance while Asylum was on cooldown.
- **A ground-placed action is no longer fired before it is ready.** The action watcher could send a ground-target placement for a replacement action that was still on cooldown; it now checks readiness first.
- Merges upstream WrathCombo changes through 2026-10-14 (9 commits). The automatic regen and shield checks on the focus target now use the plugin's own status lookup, ending an ambiguity with the shared library's lookup of the same name.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.305 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **Beastmaster in the Crucible of the Unbroken, Abaddon Piece: the rotation no longer stands idle while a Morpho is alive.** The Abaddon was held back from the start of the fight until every Morpho was gone, and the Morphos themselves are never attacked, so for as long as a Morpho lived (over a minute in a recorded fight) the Abaddon was the only enemy and nothing was left that the rotation was allowed to hit: no damage and no aggro while the Morphos confused the character. Intended behaviour in this piece: the Drake and the Barbmoles are killed first, as before; once the Abaddon is the only enemy left it is attacked and chipped down to 35% of its health, and held there while any Morpho is alive, so it is never killed ahead of the Morphos it feeds on; once the last Morpho is gone it is attacked to the end. Eggs and Morphos as targets are still never attacked, and the Gigantis gel rule is unchanged.
- The Abaddon's Regen (Rehabilitation, one minute, renewed each time it eats a Morpho) is deliberately not dispelled: Quelling Wave never removed it in the recorded casts (15 casts on the Abaddon, the buff always ran its full minute), so the rotation does not spend casts on it. XIVCombo for very lazy players.","InternalName":"GluttonyCombo","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.4.310","Changelog":"v1.0.4.311 (2026-10-18) [testing]
- **Deep Dungeon (Palace of the Dead): the sustaining potion is spent inside a behemoth's Ecliptic Meteor window whatever the health slider says.** The floor-180 meteor takes roughly 80% of maximum health, so a potion held back for after the hit is wasted. The gate now treats the meteor window itself as a heal window and rolls the potion in it; the preset toggle, item readiness and the no-Rehabilitation check all still apply, and the health slider keeps ruling everywhere else. A behemoth tracker recognises the two floor-180 behemoths by name and watches the boss's cast and health for the meteor threshold, exposing a hold band (while the cast nears the threshold) and the window (the cast itself) to the job modules below.
- **Ninja: Shade Shift is banked for the Ecliptic Meteor and pressed in the window.** While the behemoth nears its meteor threshold the shield is no longer spent on its own health or incoming-damage triggers; in the window itself it presses even at full health.
- **Summoner: Radiant Aegis banks and presses around the Ecliptic Meteor.** The overcap rule holds the second charge while the behemoth nears the threshold instead of burning it early; the maintain rule keeps a shield up through the window even above its health slider.
- **Black Mage: Manaward is banked for the Ecliptic Meteor in solo play.** The own-health trigger is held while the behemoth nears the threshold; the incoming-damage trigger still presses the ward for the cast itself, so the window stays covered.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.310 (2026-10-17)

- NIN: fixed a Kassatsu sync issue.
- DTR bar entry: right-click now opens the UI; the auto-rotation toggle moved to left-click.
- PvP: fixed hotbar saving writing to the wrong slot.
- SAM: fixed the FRU opener.
- MCH: removed an unused target setting; job config cleanups across many jobs.

v1.0.4.308 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- Telemetry only, no behaviour change: the Crucible decision log line (CR|) now carries the inputs the offline replay could not rebuild from the rest of the line - the target's invulnerability flag, the readiness of the Beastmaster's long cooldowns (the three horns, Shield Charge, Rally, Cheer, Beast Mode and the rest) as a bitmap, the health potion count, the player's current and maximum health, GCD and weave readiness, the in-combat and casting state, and whether Morphos or other enemies are still up. The offline replay tool reads these fields and replays the Crucible hold rules from them, so more of a recorded fight can be replayed faithfully.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.307 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **Beastmaster in the Crucible of the Unbroken, King Ahriman Piece: the Final Hourglass is no longer broken at the moment that points the Death cone at the character.** Breaking the hourglass makes the needle fire Death, a 23-yard cone along the needle's heading at its next tick, and Death puts Doom on whatever stands in it: a 6-second countdown that ends in certain death and that no cleanse, dispel or item removes. The needle ticks every 1.56 seconds and turns a quarter turn after each tick, and the character stands bound beside the hourglass, so a break lands in the cone about one time in four. The recorded runs show it: Death hit the character in 6 of 12 roulettes and every Doom ended in death. The rotation used to break the hourglass as fast as possible whatever the needle did. Now, once the hourglass is low enough for a single hit to break it (75% of its health or less), the weaponskill is held whenever a needle tick that the break could precede points at the character, and goes out the moment none does; the needle points at the character a quarter of the time, so the wait is at most one turn of the needle (about 6 seconds). The hold gives up 12 seconds after the hourglass appears, and does nothing at all when the needle cannot be read, which leaves the previous behaviour.
- **The log records every turn of the needle (`NE|` lines: the needle's heading, the hourglass's health, the hourglass's age, and the character's bearing and distance from the needle).**
- Doom itself cannot be removed. The game marks the Crucible's Doom as not cleansable ("Certain death when counter reaches zero"): no beast action (Ultrasonics, Scouring Ash, Quelling Wave) and no Crucible item removes it, so the cleanse path correctly stays idle. Its Crucible sources are Mortal Ray and the Ahriman gaze (Taurus Piece; the lit floor tiles clear it), the Dirty Eye's Mortal Gaze (looking away avoids it) and the King Ahriman Piece's Death (fixed here); Soulreaper's Armor is the only item that resists Doom.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.306 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **White Mage: Temperance and Divine Caress are now handled as the two separate actions they are.** Since the pair was split, the heal combos watched for the Divine Grace buff and pressed whatever Temperance had turned into. Now Temperance itself is used when it is ready - in the single-target, area and simple heal modes and in the raidwide features alike - and Divine Caress is pressed on its own when it is ready. The area-of-effect simple heal mode gains a Divine Caress step it did not have, and the Asylum replacement mode now tries Asylum first, then Temperance, then Divine Caress, instead of preferring Temperance while Asylum was on cooldown.
- **A ground-placed action is no longer fired before it is ready.** The action watcher could send a ground-target placement for a replacement action that was still on cooldown; it now checks readiness first.
- Merges upstream WrathCombo changes through 2026-10-14 (9 commits). The automatic regen and shield checks on the focus target now use the plugin's own status lookup, ending an ambiguity with the shared library's lookup of the same name.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.305 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **Beastmaster in the Crucible of the Unbroken, Abaddon Piece: the rotation no longer stands idle while a Morpho is alive.** The Abaddon was held back from the start of the fight until every Morpho was gone, and the Morphos themselves are never attacked, so for as long as a Morpho lived (over a minute in a recorded fight) the Abaddon was the only enemy and nothing was left that the rotation was allowed to hit: no damage and no aggro while the Morphos confused the character. Intended behaviour in this piece: the Drake and the Barbmoles are killed first, as before; once the Abaddon is the only enemy left it is attacked and chipped down to 35% of its health, and held there while any Morpho is alive, so it is never killed ahead of the Morphos it feeds on; once the last Morpho is gone it is attacked to the end. Eggs and Morphos as targets are still never attacked, and the Gigantis gel rule is unchanged.
- The Abaddon's Regen (Rehabilitation, one minute, renewed each time it eats a Morpho) is deliberately not dispelled: Quelling Wave never removed it in the recorded casts (15 casts on the Abaddon, the buff always ran its full minute), so the rotation does not spend casts on it. The Drake's Blaze Spikes are still dispelled.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. XIVCombo for very lazy players.","InternalName":"GluttonyCombo","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.4.310","Changelog":"v1.0.4.312 (2026-10-19) [testing]
- **White Mage and Astrologian: the timed raidwide AoE regen (Medica II/Medica III, Aspected Helios/Helios Conjunction) now casts once per raidwide.** The scheduled cast that follows the raidwide's damage burst is the only one: while that cast is timed up, the earlier auto-detection no longer fires the same heal as well, and a cast that landed before the burst is not followed by the same regen again while its heal-over-time is still active. After the regen expires, the heal is available as before. Scholar and Sage raidwide shields are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.311 (2026-10-18) [testing]
- **Deep Dungeon (Palace of the Dead): the sustaining potion is spent inside a behemoth's Ecliptic Meteor window whatever the health slider says.** The floor-180 meteor takes roughly 80% of maximum health, so a potion held back for after the hit is wasted. The gate now treats the meteor window itself as a heal window and rolls the potion in it; the preset toggle, item readiness and the no-Rehabilitation check all still apply, and the health slider keeps ruling everywhere else. A behemoth tracker recognises the two floor-180 behemoths by name and watches the boss's cast and health for the meteor threshold, exposing a hold band (while the cast nears the threshold) and the window (the cast itself) to the job modules below.
- **Ninja: Shade Shift is banked for the Ecliptic Meteor and pressed in the window.** While the behemoth nears its meteor threshold the shield is no longer spent on its own health or incoming-damage triggers; in the window itself it presses even at full health.
- **Summoner: Radiant Aegis banks and presses around the Ecliptic Meteor.** The overcap rule holds the second charge while the behemoth nears the threshold instead of burning it early; the maintain rule keeps a shield up through the window even above its health slider.
- **Black Mage: Manaward is banked for the Ecliptic Meteor in solo play.** The own-health trigger is held while the behemoth nears the threshold; the incoming-damage trigger still presses the ward for the cast itself, so the window stays covered.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.310 (2026-10-17)

- NIN: fixed a Kassatsu sync issue.
- DTR bar entry: right-click now opens the UI; the auto-rotation toggle moved to left-click.
- PvP: fixed hotbar saving writing to the wrong slot.
- SAM: fixed the FRU opener.
- MCH: removed an unused target setting; job config cleanups across many jobs.

v1.0.4.308 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- Telemetry only, no behaviour change: the Crucible decision log line (CR|) now carries the inputs the offline replay could not rebuild from the rest of the line - the target's invulnerability flag, the readiness of the Beastmaster's long cooldowns (the three horns, Shield Charge, Rally, Cheer, Beast Mode and the rest) as a bitmap, the health potion count, the player's current and maximum health, GCD and weave readiness, the in-combat and casting state, and whether Morphos or other enemies are still up. The offline replay tool reads these fields and replays the Crucible hold rules from them, so more of a recorded fight can be replayed faithfully.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.307 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **Beastmaster in the Crucible of the Unbroken, King Ahriman Piece: the Final Hourglass is no longer broken at the moment that points the Death cone at the character.** Breaking the hourglass makes the needle fire Death, a 23-yard cone along the needle's heading at its next tick, and Death puts Doom on whatever stands in it: a 6-second countdown that ends in certain death and that no cleanse, dispel or item removes. The needle ticks every 1.56 seconds and turns a quarter turn after each tick, and the character stands bound beside the hourglass, so a break lands in the cone about one time in four. The recorded runs show it: Death hit the character in 6 of 12 roulettes and every Doom ended in death. The rotation used to break the hourglass as fast as possible whatever the needle did. Now, once the hourglass is low enough for a single hit to break it (75% of its health or less), the weaponskill is held whenever a needle tick that the break could precede points at the character, and goes out the moment none does; the needle points at the character a quarter of the time, so the wait is at most one turn of the needle (about 6 seconds). The hold gives up 12 seconds after the hourglass appears, and does nothing at all when the needle cannot be read, which leaves the previous behaviour.
- **The log records every turn of the needle (`NE|` lines: the needle's heading, the hourglass's health, the hourglass's age, and the character's bearing and distance from the needle).**
- Doom itself cannot be removed. The game marks the Crucible's Doom as not cleansable ("Certain death when counter reaches zero"): no beast action (Ultrasonics, Scouring Ash, Quelling Wave) and no Crucible item removes it, so the cleanse path correctly stays idle. Its Crucible sources are Mortal Ray and the Ahriman gaze (Taurus Piece; the lit floor tiles clear it), the Dirty Eye's Mortal Gaze (looking away avoids it) and the King Ahriman Piece's Death (fixed here); Soulreaper's Armor is the only item that resists Doom.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.306 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **White Mage: Temperance and Divine Caress are now handled as the two separate actions they are.** Since the pair was split, the heal combos watched for the Divine Grace buff and pressed whatever Temperance had turned into. Now Temperance itself is used when it is ready - in the single-target, area and simple heal modes and in the raidwide features alike - and Divine Caress is pressed on its own when it is ready. The area-of-effect simple heal mode gains a Divine Caress step it did not have, and the Asylum replacement mode now tries Asylum first, then Temperance, then Divine Caress, instead of preferring Temperance while Asylum was on cooldown.
- **A ground-placed action is no longer fired before it is ready.** The action watcher could send a ground-target placement for a replacement action that was still on cooldown; it now checks readiness first.
- Merges upstream WrathCombo changes through 2026-10-14 (9 commits). The automatic regen and shield checks on the focus target now use the plugin's own status lookup, ending an ambiguity with the shared library's lookup of the same name.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. The end-of-match results screen still waits for you by design - that is the one click after a match. v0.3.7.0: Chi is now fully automated. The picker layout is dumped once per session to the log folder so shape-specific selection can be refined against real captures. Call prompts now prefer the newest board addition over a possibly stale pond tile (the live log claimed 6z/dragon while the actual Pon was 9m), and the log records the last discard tile/seat. A v5 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging. v0.3.4.0: Fix the self-kan freeze. A Kan/Pass bar at state 6 is ignored and the normal discard proceeds instead of firing a Pass callback the client ignores. Diagnostic bundles now include the actual Dalamud plugin config file from pluginConfigs. v0.3.2.0: State 15 is now treated as the generic other-players state unless real call buttons are present, state 22 (forced riichi discard) is automated, and state 27 (between-hands result/score) is recognised instead of showing stale advice. Overlay/advice are now gated to actual decision states, and diagnostic bundles can read the Dalamud log while it is open. v0.3.1.0: Auto-play and file logging are now on by default, /mjadv session starts a clean logged session, and /mjadv bundle packages the recent JSONL logs, config, layouts, Dalamud log tail and a full last-read snapshot into one zip. Replays the client's FireCallback protocol for discards, calls, riichi, ron/tsumo and result advancement, using the reference solver's live-verified handshake and timing guards. Off by default; /mjadv auto [on/off] or /mjadv stop toggles it. Pon/ron/tsumo/riichi are enabled by default, chi and kan are opt-in, the chi shape picker pauses for a manual choice, and the new-hand screen is never auto-advanced. Added /mjadv hand and /mjadv options diagnostics. v0.2.0.2: Keep the previous wall count, so the wall-jump half of new-hand detection actually fires. v0.2.0.1: Reset the pond baselines at the start of a new hand, so the first discard of the hand is tracked and the first call prompt gets the right claimed tile. v0.2.0.0: Meld containers now read by default (112-115 families), with a fail-closed check against our own called-meld count. Own meld tiles are recovered from hand deltas when nodes are unavailable, so ukeire no longer counts tiles already in a call. Riichi detection is marker-node only; the dead rotation and score-drop paths are gone. One node-tree walk per read instead of up to seven. Fixed dead hands getting a nonzero win rate and Pass inventing a yaku path. Red-five decoding accepts both absolute and alias ids. Removed the obsolete fold-threshold setting. Setup window no longer reopens every launch. Discard piles and meld strips are found automatically; the node tools are only a fallback.","Changelog":"v0.4.1.0: Advanced-table defence. Cross-seat genbutsu now uses the pond lengths captured at the instant a riichi marker appears; the old turn-count shortcut broke once calls shortened ponds and could mark a tile discarded before the riichi as safe. Two declared riichi also force a fold for any hand that is not tenpai, overriding the placement chase. The simulator now records the same declaration snapshots: over 1,000 hands the defence fix moved deal-in rate from 10.3% to 9.5% and average points from -22 to +17, while the double-riichi rail was neutral there because the simulation has no placement stance. Live Advanced trial on 0.4.0.0 finished 1st, 4th, then leading when stopped; the 4th lost two deal-ins to one riichi player, the second 12,000 while two were in riichi. v0.4.0.0: Exact scoring core. Completed hands are now scored by yaku, fu, dora and the payment table (closed and open, riichi through yakuman), and the offline simulator uses that scoring for win legality and payouts. Ready-hand valuation was built and benchmarked but stays out of live decisions: over 1,500 simulated hands, mixing exact tenpai values with the existing one-away estimate cut the win rate from 15.4% to 8.1%, so the value scale must be unified for every shanten first. Advice is memoised per table state so the overlay and controller do not recompute the same decision. v0.3.10.0: Silent-endgame defence. The threat model measured a silent opponent as at most 19% likely tenpai, so on a table with no riichi and no melds every safety rule stayed off - the controller pushed one-away hands with 6-9 tiles left to draw into damaten twice in one match (4,200 and 2,200 deal-ins) and paid full tsumo on 14,300 and 20,000 hands. Silent seats now take on a readiness floor that rises from zero at wall 32 to a concrete threat at wall 16, arming the existing late-wall fold and per-tile safety ranking on quiet tables. v0.3.9.0: Chi freeze fixed. The shape-selection dialog ignores scripted call picks (confirmed by the first picker dump), so chi now only fires when exactly one shape is possible - that path completes with no dialog. Multi-shape chi passes instead of stalling; the pass log records how many shapes were declined. v0.3.8.0: Late-wall defence. When an opponent is a concrete threat and the wall is down to the last four go-arounds, the controller folds any hand that is not tenpai instead of pushing a 1-shanten no-riichi hand. This was the 12,000 deal-in in the first match. Diagnostic bundles now also include chi picker dumps. The end-of-match results screen still waits for you by design - that is the one click after a match. v0.3.7.0: Chi is now fully automated. The controller calls chi when the advisor ranks it best, and if the client shows the shape-selection surface it fires the first variant and re-evaluates the hand. The picker layout is dumped once per session to the log folder so shape-specific selection can be refined against real captures. A v6 config migration enables chi. v0.3.6.0: Read each opponent meld strip independently. A hidden empty strip for one quiet seat no longer suppresses every visible meld on the table, so the threat model sees called sets when they exist. This is a readiness/defence accuracy change; automation logic is unchanged. v0.3.5.0: Fix the second freeze. A complete open hand is no longer assumed to be a legal tsumo: the controller checks for an actual yaku and keeps discarding when there is none. Call prompts now prefer the newest board addition over a possibly stale pond tile (the live log claimed 6z/dragon while the actual Pon was 9m), and the log records the last discard tile/seat. A v5 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging. v0.3.4.0: Fix the self-kan freeze. A Kan/Pass bar at state 6 is ignored and the normal discard proceeds instead of firing a Pass callback the client ignores. Session stats are preserved after /mjadv stop so the bundle still shows the run, and a v4 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging for the next launch. v0.3.3.0: Reset the exposed tuning sliders to the fitted win-rate defaults (base hand value 1300, deal-in 5200, noten 1500, opponent hand 4000) with a one-time v3 config migration. Diagnostic bundles now include the actual Dalamud plugin config file from pluginConfigs. v0.3.2.0: State 15 is now treated as the generic other-players state unless real call buttons are present, state 22 (forced riichi discard) is automated, and state 27 (between-hands result/score) is recognised instead of showing stale advice. Overlay/advice are now gated to actual decision states, and diagnostic bundles can read the Dalamud log while it is open. v0.3.1.0: Auto-play and file logging are now on by default, /mjadv session starts a clean logged session, and /mjadv bundle packages the recent JSONL logs, config, layouts, Dalamud log tail and a full last-read snapshot into one zip. Status changes are now logged as auto-status records. v0.3.0.1: Re-arm auto-play on a state change even when the hand happens to repeat, and wait for the Riichi/Pass prompt to close before cutting the riichi tile. v0.3.0.0: Optional auto-play. Replays the client's FireCallback protocol for discards, calls, riichi, ron/tsumo and result advancement, using the reference solver's live-verified handshake and timing guards. Off by default; /mjadv auto [on/off] or /mjadv stop toggles it. Pon/ron/tsumo/riichi are enabled by default, chi and kan are opt-in, the chi shape picker pauses for a manual choice, and the new-hand screen is never auto-advanced. Added /mjadv hand and /mjadv options diagnostics. v0.2.0.2: Keep the previous wall count, so the wall-jump half of new-hand detection actually fires. v0.2.0.1: Reset the pond baselines at the start of a new hand, so the first discard of the hand is tracked and the first call prompt gets the right claimed tile. v0.2.0.0: Meld containers now read by default (112-115 families), with a fail-closed check against our own called-meld count. Own meld tiles are recovered from hand deltas when nodes are unavailable, so ukeire no longer counts tiles already in a call. Riichi detection is marker-node only; the dead rotation and score-drop paths are gone. One node-tree walk per read instead of up to seven. Fixed dead hands getting a nonzero win rate and Pass inventing a yaku path. Red-five decoding accepts both absolute and alias ids. Removed the obsolete fold-threshold setting. Setup window no longer reopens every launch. Added /mjadv melds diagnostics and richer log records.","DownloadLinkInstall":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","LoadRequiredState":0,"LoadSync":false,"CanUnloadAsync":false,"LoadPriority":0,"AcceptsFeedback":true,"IsHide":false,"_SourceId":"dexcss-dalamudplugins","_SourceName":"dexcss / DalamudPlugins","_SourceUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dexcss/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json","_Category":"automation"}
