This was the 12,000 deal-in in the first match. Diagnostic bundles now also include chi picker dumps. The end-of-match results screen still waits for you by design - that is the one click after a match. v0.3.7.0: Chi is now fully automated. The controller calls chi when the advisor ranks it best, and if the client shows the shape-selection surface it fires the first variant and re-evaluates the hand. The picker layout is dumped once per session to the log folder so shape-specific selection can be refined against real captures. This is a readiness/defence accuracy change; automation logic is unchanged. v0.3.5.0: Fix the second freeze. A complete open hand is no longer assumed to be a legal tsumo: the controller checks for an actual yaku and keeps discarding when there is none. Call prompts now prefer the newest board addition over a possibly stale pond tile (the live log claimed 6z/dragon while the actual Pon was 9m), and the log records the last discard tile/seat. A v5 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging. v0.3.4.0: Fix the self-kan freeze. A Kan/Pass bar at state 6 is ignored and the normal discard proceeds instead of firing a Pass callback the client ignores. Session stats are preserved after /mjadv stop so the bundle still shows the run, and a v4 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging for the next launch. v0.3.3.0: Reset the exposed tuning sliders to the fitted win-rate defaults (base hand value 1300, deal-in 5200, noten 1500, opponent hand 4000) with a one-time v3 config migration. Diagnostic bundles now include the actual Dalamud plugin config file from pluginConfigs. v0.3.2.0: State 15 is now treated as the generic other-players state unless real call buttons are present, state 22 (forced riichi discard) is automated, and state 27 (between-hands result/score) is recognised instead of showing stale advice. Overlay/advice are now gated to actual decision states, and diagnostic bundles can read the Dalamud log while it is open. v0.3.1.0: Auto-play and file logging are now on by default, /mjadv session starts a clean logged session, and /mjadv bundle packages the recent JSONL logs, config, layouts, Dalamud log tail and a full last-read snapshot into one zip. Off by default; /mjadv auto [on/off] or /mjadv stop toggles it. Pon/ron/tsumo/riichi are enabled by default, chi and kan are opt-in, the chi shape picker pauses for a manual choice, and the new-hand screen is never auto-advanced. Added /mjadv hand and /mjadv options diagnostics. v0.2.0.2: Keep the previous wall count, so the wall-jump half of new-hand detection actually fires. v0.2.0.1: Reset the pond baselines at the start of a new hand, so the first discard of the hand is tracked and the first call prompt gets the right claimed tile. v0.2.0.0: Meld containers now read by default (112-115 families), with a fail-closed check against our own called-meld count. Own meld tiles are recovered from hand deltas when nodes are unavailable, so ukeire no longer counts tiles already in a call. Riichi detection is marker-node only; the dead rotation and score-drop paths are gone. One node-tree walk per read instead of up to seven. /deepducking resume [resume retained local run after readiness checks]
/deepducking nextstop [exit after next boss]
/deepducking ns [exit after next boss]
/deepducking stop [FULL STOP; persist local lock across reloads; stay in duty]
/deepducking reset-stop [clear eligible FULL STOP after cleanup; do not start]
/deepducking status [print local status]
/deepducking inspect [record read-only client and native observations]
/deepducking saves [open Saves]
/deepducking saves info <dungeon> [inspect native saves]

{"Author":"Akari","Name":"Mahjong Advisor","AcceptsFeedback":true,"ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.4.3.0","CanUnloadAsync":false,"CategoryTags":["Utility"],"Changelog":"v0.4.3.0: Result-screen retry. The result panel can swallow the first advance callback while it animates; the controller fired it twice and then its acted guard blocked every retry, leaving the screen waiting indefinitely (live Advanced freeze, state 29 unresolved for 12s). Advances now retry every 2.5 seconds while the result state persists, capped at 8 attempts so the deliberately manual match-end screen is not spammed. v0.4.2.0: Match-level tuning. A full hanchan evaluator now plays East+South with real score accounting, dealer rotation, honcha, riichi sticks and placement, and 120 paired matches showed the old risk settings were too passive. Win value 1800 and deal-in cost 4000 beat 1300/5200 on identical deals (average place 2.55 vs 2.65, more firsts, fewer fourths) with the deal-in rate unchanged at 9.3%. A v7 config migration applies the new values. Riichi hand value and placement stance were also tested and left unchanged - both were flat across 60-match arms. v0.4.1.0: Advanced-table defence. Cross-seat genbutsu now uses the pond lengths captured at the instant a riichi marker appears; the old turn-count shortcut broke once calls shortened ponds and could mark a tile discarded before the riichi as safe. Two declared riichi also force a fold for any hand that is not tenpai, overriding the placement chase. The simulator now records the same declaration snapshots: over 1,000 hands the defence fix moved deal-in rate from 10.3% to 9.5% and average points from -22 to +17, while the double-riichi rail was neutral there because the simulation has no placement stance. Live Advanced trial on 0.4.0.0 finished 1st, 4th, then leading when stopped; the 4th lost two deal-ins to one riichi player, the second 12,000 while two were in riichi. v0.4.0.0: Exact scoring core. Completed hands are now scored by yaku, fu, dora and the payment table (closed and open, riichi through yakuman), and the offline simulator uses that scoring for win legality and payouts. Ready-hand valuation was built and benchmarked but stays out of live decisions: over 1,500 simulated hands, mixing exact tenpai values with the existing one-away estimate cut the win rate from 15.4% to 8.1%, so the value scale must be unified for every shanten first. Advice is memoised per table state so the overlay and controller do not recompute the same decision. v0.3.10.0: Silent-endgame defence. The threat model measured a silent opponent as at most 19% likely tenpai, so on a table with no riichi and no melds every safety rule stayed off - the controller pushed one-away hands with 6-9 tiles left to draw into damaten twice in one match (4,200 and 2,200 deal-ins) and paid full tsumo on 14,300 and 20,000 hands. Silent seats now take on a readiness floor that rises from zero at wall 32 to a concrete threat at wall 16, arming the existing late-wall fold and per-tile safety ranking on quiet tables. v0.3.9.0: Chi freeze fixed. The shape-selection dialog ignores scripted call picks (confirmed by the first picker dump), so chi now only fires when exactly one shape is possible - that path completes with no dialog. Multi-shape chi passes instead of stalling; the pass log records how many shapes were declined. v0.3.8.0: Late-wall defence. When an opponent is a concrete threat and the wall is down to the last four go-arounds, the controller folds any hand that is not tenpai instead of pushing a 1-shanten no-riichi hand. This was the 12,000 deal-in in the first match. Diagnostic bundles now also include chi picker dumps. The end-of-match results screen still waits for you by design - that is the one click after a match. v0.3.7.0: Chi is now fully automated. The controller calls chi when the advisor ranks it best, and if the client shows the shape-selection surface it fires the first variant and re-evaluates the hand. The picker layout is dumped once per session to the log folder so shape-specific selection can be refined against real captures. A v6 config migration enables chi. v0.3.6.0: Read each opponent meld strip independently. A hidden empty strip for one quiet seat no longer suppresses every visible meld on the table, so the threat model sees called sets when they exist. This is a readiness/defence accuracy change; automation logic is unchanged. v0.3.5.0: Fix the second freeze. A complete open hand is no longer assumed to be a legal tsumo: the controller checks for an actual yaku and keeps discarding when there is none. Call prompts now prefer the newest board addition over a possibly stale pond tile (the live log claimed 6z/dragon while the actual Pon was 9m), and the log records the last discard tile/seat. A v5 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging. v0.3.4.0: Fix the self-kan freeze. A Kan/Pass bar at state 6 is ignored and the normal discard proceeds instead of firing a Pass callback the client ignores. Session stats are preserved after /mjadv stop so the bundle still shows the run, and a v4 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging for the next launch. v0.3.3.0: Reset the exposed tuning sliders to the fitted win-rate defaults (base hand value 1300, deal-in 5200, noten 1500, opponent hand 4000) with a one-time v3 config migration. Diagnostic bundles now include the actual Dalamud plugin config file from pluginConfigs. v0.3.2.0: State 15 is now treated as the generic other-players state unless real call buttons are present, state 22 (forced riichi discard) is automated, and state 27 (between-hands result/score) is recognised instead of showing stale advice. Overlay/advice are now gated to actual decision states, and diagnostic bundles can read the Dalamud log while it is open. v0.3.1.0: Auto-play and file logging are now on by default, /mjadv session starts a clean logged session, and /mjadv bundle packages the recent JSONL logs, config, layouts, Dalamud log tail and a full last-read snapshot into one zip. Status changes are now logged as auto-status records. v0.3.0.1: Re-arm auto-play on a state change even when the hand happens to repeat, and wait for the Riichi/Pass prompt to close before cutting the riichi tile. v0.3.0.0: Optional auto-play. Replays the client's FireCallback protocol for discards, calls, riichi, ron/tsumo and result advancement, using the reference solver's live-verified handshake and timing guards. Off by default; /mjadv auto [on/off] or /mjadv stop toggles it. Pon/ron/tsumo/riichi are enabled by default, chi and kan are opt-in, the chi shape picker pauses for a manual choice, and the new-hand screen is never auto-advanced. Added /mjadv hand and /mjadv options diagnostics. v0.2.0.2: Keep the previous wall count, so the wall-jump half of new-hand detection actually fires. v0.2.0.1: Reset the pond baselines at the start of a new hand, so the first discard of the hand is tracked and the first call prompt gets the right claimed tile. v0.2.0.0: Meld containers now read by default (112-115 families), with a fail-closed check against our own called-meld count. Own meld tiles are recovered from hand deltas when nodes are unavailable, so ukeire no longer counts tiles already in a call. Riichi detection is marker-node only; the dead rotation and score-drop paths are gone. One node-tree walk per read instead of up to seven. Fixed dead hands getting a nonzero win rate and Pass inventing a yaku path. Red-five decoding accepts both absolute and alias ids. Removed the obsolete fold-threshold setting. Setup window no longer reopens every launch. Added /mjadv melds diagnostics and richer log records.","DalamudApiLevel":15,"Description":"Reads your Doman Mahjong hand, discards, dora, scores and called melds, then ranks each discard by hand speed against deal-in risk. {"Author":"Valenth Siveria","Name":"I Am Ready","Punchline":"Automatically accept or decline Duty Finder ready checks based on a configurable counter.","Description":"# I Am Ready

**I Am Ready** is a Dalamud plugin for Final Fantasy XIV that automatically accepts or declines Party and Alliance Ready Checks based on a customizable counter. 

Whether you are stepping away for a moment or just tired of clicking, this plugin handles ready checks for you while mimicking human reaction times.

## ✨ Features

* **Auto-Answer Ready Checks:** Automatically clicks "Yes" or "No" when a ready check appears.
* **Configurable "Yes" Counter:** Set a specific number of times you want to automatically answer "Yes". Once that limit is reached, the plugin will automatically start answering "No" to prevent pulling when you are actually away.
* **Natural Delay:** Enable a randomized delay (0.7 to 2.5 seconds) before the plugin answers, making it look like a natural human reaction.
* **Smart Chat Triggers (Regex):** Add custom text phrases to the plugin. If someone says one of these phrases in Party or Alliance chat (e.g., "reset", "pulling"), your counter will automatically reset back to zero.
* **Bilingual Support:** The user interface is available in both English and German.

## 🚀 Usage

1. Type `/iar` in the in-game chat to open the configuration window.
2. Click the **Inactive/Active** button at the top to turn the auto-responder on or off.
3. Adjust the **Yes Count** slider. For example, if set to `5`, the plugin will answer "Yes" to the next 5 ready checks, and "No" to any checks after that.
4. Click the **Start** button at any time to manually reset your current counter back to zero.

### Chat Triggers (Regex Patterns)
At the bottom of the window, you can expand the **Regex Patterns** section. Here you can add simple words or complex regex patterns. 
If the plugin reads a matching message in your Party or Cross-World Party chat, it will instantly reset your counter to zero, assuming a new pull or instance is starting!

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"LazyCrucible","Punchline":"Crucible of the Unbroken familiar picks, filled in for every fight","Description":"For the Beastmaster duty Crucible of the Unbroken. Includes the beast-pick advisor for every board and a read-only recorder that writes each Crucible screen to the Dalamud log. Use /lazycrucible to open.","InternalName":"LazyCrucible","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.9.5","TestingAssemblyVersion":"0.1.9.16","TestingDalamudApiLevel":15,"Changelog":"v0.1.9.16 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **"Score: three familiars" run-roster mode, off by default.** For score runs. A run roster of one to three familiars scores the Beast Squad III bonus on every board, so with the option on the run roster is the best three familiars for the whole board instead of the board's full roster. The three are chosen from the familiars you own and that are not knocked out: they cover as many of the board's required interrupt, dispel and cleanse needs as any three can, then the damage the board calls to be blunted, then three of one kin when that costs no required cover (the Gambit bonus), then the rest by points. A roster of three saved for a different board is rewritten for the board you enter. Whatever the three cannot answer on the board is named on the window's summary line; nothing pops up. With three or fewer familiars the game registers the battlehorns itself, so the plugin leaves them alone. Found in the settings window and the Lazy Hub as "Score: three familiars".
- With the option off, nothing changes. While AutoDuty drives the run roster the plugin stands by there, option on or off.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.9.15 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **Mitigation in the horn picks.** Fights with a damage wall now field a familiar that blunts it, ranked below every interrupt, dispel and cleanse need, and counted only for a familiar above the danger HP line. Durga's Atomic Ray gets a magic answer (drake's Smoldering Scales, pugil's Water Wall or a Scalekin's Scaleskin); Borgny gets coblyn's Vulcanize for the poison plus a magic answer; Gargoyle's Sweeping Evisceration gets a physical answer (a Beastkin's Beastskin, coblyn's Vulcanize or adamantoise's Harden Shell). The fight guide lists these under "Calls for".
- One telemetry line per fight names the team on the horns and the needs it cannot answer (`uncovered=`).
- **Works with AutoDuty.** While AutoDuty runs, it handles the run roster, shop, treasure, spoils and campsite itself, so the plugin stands by there; the battlehorns are AutoDuty's only with its "Fight picks" on, and the plugin picks them otherwise. AutoDuty's active profile is read through AutoDuty's own interface (its config file when that is unavailable), never changed; when neither can be read, every screen stands by, as before. The window shows one quiet line naming the screens it is standing by on.
- **No more corrections on top of AutoDuty's familiar picks.** AutoDuty re-applied its own picks every time, so they never reached a fight.
- **Fight guide: the Snarl -> Parting Blow advice is gone** (Parting Blow no longer dodges a hit since the September 17 hotfix). Plain tankbusters say to let a familiar with enough HP take them under Snarl; poisoning ones (Deadly Thrust, Cold Caress, Toxic Vomit) say to Parting Blow right after the hit so the poison leaves with the familiar; Gargoyle's Sweeping Evisceration says to save the Blink tome for it.
- Item values: Beastly Knife is valued like the elemental axes; Hero's Crown counts its Excellence proc (9 s of nullified attacks); Rapid Recast gear is valued; reraise items are worth a little less at Third Degree.
- **Patch 7.57: battlehorns the game registered itself (teams of three or fewer) are left alone**; a knocked-out member of a three-familiar team is no longer toggled off the horns.
- **Patch 7.57: the board's degree survives a job change** (the game now keeps the Crucible Mode until logout), so the degree passed to Gluttony Combo is no longer reset when the character returns to Beastmaster. It is forgotten at logout.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.9.14 (2026-10-06) [testing]
- **The board's difficulty degree now reaches Gluttony Combo during a fight.** The degree is set in the lobby (by a click or by AutoDuty) and the character then zones into the duty; the plugin used to forget it at every loading screen, so a fight always read as an unknown degree. It is now kept across loading screens and still forgotten when the Beastmaster job is left or the plugin unloads.

v0.1.9.13 (2026-10-06) [testing]
- **The board's difficulty degree is now read and shared with Gluttony Combo.** The Crucible board layout reports the degree whenever it is set, by a click or by AutoDuty; the plugin keeps the last one (Standard, First, Second or Third) and offers it to Gluttony Combo 1.0.4.288 or newer, which uses it to price the hits a familiar or the character will take. The degree is forgotten when the Beastmaster job is left, and until the first time it is set the plugin reports none. The change is logged as one `PS|` line (`note=degree`).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.9.12 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The run-roster need-coverage correction no longer fires while AutoDuty drives the screen.** AutoDuty re-asserts its own roster through a confirm sequence that removes unfamiliar rows one per pass and holds its acceptance until they are gone; every correction written on that surface was removed before entry, and the acceptance follows the build's last pick by about half a second with nothing the plugin can observe in between — a guess there only spent the correction budget on rows that were going to be removed anyway. The surface is now left to AutoDuty entirely. The battlehorn surface is unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.9.11 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The run-roster need-coverage correction now waits for the roster itself to stop changing.** The previous fix judged a settled roster by edit timestamps, but the roster AutoDuty builds is driven through the monster notebook, whose selection writes never register as edits — so the timestamp stayed at screen-open while the build was still adding picks, and the correction still fired mid-build, where AutoDuty's continuing build and its confirm passes removed the added rows. The correction is now due only once the selected roster has been unchanged for 1.5 seconds — what the plugin sees every frame — never on an empty roster, and it still re-arms after any later AutoDuty write. The screen log's roster needfix line now also carries the age of the last edit (`adedit=`), the roster's quiet time (`adstb=`) and the selected count (`flutes=`).

{"Author":"Akari","Name":"Mahjong Advisor","InternalName":"Mahjong.Advisor.Plugin","AssemblyVersion":"0.4.3.0","TestingAssemblyVersion":"0.4.3.0","IsTestingExclusive":false,"RepoUrl":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor","ApplicableVersion":"any","DalamudApiLevel":15,"TestingDalamudApiLevel":15,"MinimumDalamudVersion":null,"Tags":["mahjong","doman","gold-saucer","auto-play","advisor"],"CategoryTags":["Utility"],"Punchline":"Discard advice and optional auto-play for Doman Mahjong.","Description":"Reads your Doman Mahjong hand, discards, dora, scores and called melds, then ranks each discard by hand speed against deal-in risk. Auto-play and file logging are on by default in this build: sit at a casual table and it plays, then /mjadv bundle packages the logs for support. /mjadv stop or the Automation tab returns to manual suggestions instantly. Discard piles and meld strips are found automatically; the node tools are only a fallback.","Changelog":"v0.4.3.0: Result-screen retry. The result panel can swallow the first advance callback while it animates; the controller fired it twice and then its acted guard blocked every retry, leaving the screen waiting indefinitely (live Advanced freeze, state 29 unresolved for 12s). Advances now retry every 2.5 seconds while the result state persists, capped at 8 attempts so the deliberately manual match-end screen is not spammed. v0.4.2.0: Match-level tuning. A full hanchan evaluator now plays East+South with real score accounting, dealer rotation, honcha, riichi sticks and placement, and 120 paired matches showed the old risk settings were too passive. Win value 1800 and deal-in cost 4000 beat 1300/5200 on identical deals (average place 2.55 vs 2.65, more firsts, fewer fourths) with the deal-in rate unchanged at 9.3%. A v7 config migration applies the new values. Riichi hand value and placement stance were also tested and left unchanged - both were flat across 60-match arms. v0.4.1.0: Advanced-table defence. Cross-seat genbutsu now uses the pond lengths captured at the instant a riichi marker appears; the old turn-count shortcut broke once calls shortened ponds and could mark a tile discarded before the riichi as safe. Two declared riichi also force a fold for any hand that is not tenpai, overriding the placement chase. The simulator now records the same declaration snapshots: over 1,000 hands the defence fix moved deal-in rate from 10.3% to 9.5% and average points from -22 to +17, while the double-riichi rail was neutral there because the simulation has no placement stance. Live Advanced trial on 0.4.0.0 finished 1st, 4th, then leading when stopped; the 4th lost two deal-ins to one riichi player, the second 12,000 while two were in riichi. v0.4.0.0: Exact scoring core. Completed hands are now scored by yaku, fu, dora and the payment table (closed and open, riichi through yakuman), and the offline simulator uses that scoring for win legality and payouts. Ready-hand valuation was built and benchmarked but stays out of live decisions: over 1,500 simulated hands, mixing exact tenpai values with the existing one-away estimate cut the win rate from 15.4% to 8.1%, so the value scale must be unified for every shanten first. Advice is memoised per table state so the overlay and controller do not recompute the same decision. v0.3.10.0: Silent-endgame defence. The threat model measured a silent opponent as at most 19% likely tenpai, so on a table with no riichi and no melds every safety rule stayed off - the controller pushed one-away hands with 6-9 tiles left to draw into damaten twice in one match (4,200 and 2,200 deal-ins) and paid full tsumo on 14,300 and 20,000 hands. Silent seats now take on a readiness floor that rises from zero at wall 32 to a concrete threat at wall 16, arming the existing late-wall fold and per-tile safety ranking on quiet tables. v0.3.9.0: Chi freeze fixed. The shape-selection dialog ignores scripted call picks (confirmed by the first picker dump), so chi now only fires when exactly one shape is possible - that path completes with no dialog. Multi-shape chi passes instead of stalling; the pass log records how many shapes were declined. v0.3.8.0: Late-wall defence. When an opponent is a concrete threat and the wall is down to the last four go-arounds, the controller folds any hand that is not tenpai instead of pushing a 1-shanten no-riichi hand. This was the 12,000 deal-in in the first match. Diagnostic bundles now also include chi picker dumps. The end-of-match results screen still waits for you by design - that is the one click after a match. v0.3.7.0: Chi is now fully automated. The controller calls chi when the advisor ranks it best, and if the client shows the shape-selection surface it fires the first variant and re-evaluates the hand. The picker layout is dumped once per session to the log folder so shape-specific selection can be refined against real captures. A v6 config migration enables chi. v0.3.6.0: Read each opponent meld strip independently. A hidden empty strip for one quiet seat no longer suppresses every visible meld on the table, so the threat model sees called sets when they exist. This is a readiness/defence accuracy change; automation logic is unchanged. v0.3.5.0: Fix the second freeze. A complete open hand is no longer assumed to be a legal tsumo: the controller checks for an actual yaku and keeps discarding when there is none. Call prompts now prefer the newest board addition over a possibly stale pond tile (the live log claimed 6z/dragon while the actual Pon was 9m), and the log records the last discard tile/seat. A v5 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging. v0.3.4.0: Fix the self-kan freeze. A Kan/Pass bar at state 6 is ignored and the normal discard proceeds instead of firing a Pass callback the client ignores. Session stats are preserved after /mjadv stop so the bundle still shows the run, and a v4 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging for the next launch. v0.3.3.0: Reset the exposed tuning sliders to the fitted win-rate defaults (base hand value 1300, deal-in 5200, noten 1500, opponent hand 4000) with a one-time v3 config migration. Diagnostic bundles now include the actual Dalamud plugin config file from pluginConfigs. v0.3.2.0: State 15 is now treated as the generic other-players state unless real call buttons are present, state 22 (forced riichi discard) is automated, and state 27 (between-hands result/score) is recognised instead of showing stale advice. Overlay/advice are now gated to actual decision states, and diagnostic bundles can read the Dalamud log while it is open. v0.3.1.0: Auto-play and file logging are now on by default, /mjadv session starts a clean logged session, and /mjadv bundle packages the recent JSONL logs, config, layouts, Dalamud log tail and a full last-read snapshot into one zip. Status changes are now logged as auto-status records. v0.3.0.1: Re-arm auto-play on a state change even when the hand happens to repeat, and wait for the Riichi/Pass prompt to close before cutting the riichi tile. v0.3.0.0: Optional auto-play. Replays the client's FireCallback protocol for discards, calls, riichi, ron/tsumo and result advancement, using the reference solver's live-verified handshake and timing guards. Off by default; /mjadv auto [on/off] or /mjadv stop toggles it. Pon/ron/tsumo/riichi are enabled by default, chi and kan are opt-in, the chi shape picker pauses for a manual choice, and the new-hand screen is never auto-advanced. Added /mjadv hand and /mjadv options diagnostics. v0.2.0.2: Keep the previous wall count, so the wall-jump half of new-hand detection actually fires. v0.2.0.1: Reset the pond baselines at the start of a new hand, so the first discard of the hand is tracked and the first call prompt gets the right claimed tile. v0.2.0.0: Meld containers now read by default (112-115 families), with a fail-closed check against our own called-meld count. Own meld tiles are recovered from hand deltas when nodes are unavailable, so ukeire no longer counts tiles already in a call. Riichi detection is marker-node only; the dead rotation and score-drop paths are gone. One node-tree walk per read instead of up to seven. Fixed dead hands getting a nonzero win rate and Pass inventing a yaku path. Red-five decoding accepts both absolute and alias ids. Removed the obsolete fold-threshold setting. Setup window no longer reopens every launch. Added /mjadv melds diagnostics and richer log records.","DownloadLinkInstall":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","LoadRequiredState":0,"LoadSync":false,"CanUnloadAsync":false,"LoadPriority":0,"AcceptsFeedback":true,"IsHide":false,"_SourceId":"dexcss-dalamudplugins","_SourceName":"dexcss / DalamudPlugins","_SourceUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dexcss/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json","_Category":"automation"}
